rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī derives al-janb from distance, opposite kinship: it describes a stranger far from home or kin; the same root names sides and ritual impurity because of separation from purity and mosque prayer until washing.
rows.anchor: الواحدي : الجنب نعت على وزن فعل ، وأصله من الجنابة

rows.speaker: المفضل عن عاصم
rows.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal transmits from ʿĀṣim a reading with fatḥa on jīm and sukūn on nūn; it permits reading the phrase as a neighbor of the side or as an emphatic adjective.
rows.anchor: وروى المفضل عن عاصم : { والجار الجنب } بفتح الجيم وسكون النون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the variant, al-janb may mean a side, with an understood construct (the neighbor of the side), or function as an intensive adjective like generosity and munificence.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه يريد بالجنب الناحية ، ويكون التقدير : والجار ذي الجنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion at one’s side includes a travel companion, adjoining neighbor, work or study partner, or anyone who briefly sits beside one; their claim must be honored and made a means of kindness.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي صحبك بأن حصل بجنبك إما رفيقا في

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported interpretation identifies the companion at one’s side as a wife, who is with and lies beside her husband.
rows.anchor: قيل : الصاحب الجنب : المرأة فانها تكون معك وتضجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The son of the road is a traveler cut off from his home country.
rows.anchor: وهو المسافر الذي انقطع عن بلده

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A second reported interpretation takes the son of the road to mean a guest.
rows.anchor: وهو المسافر الذي انقطع عن بلده ، وقيل : الضيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kindness to enslaved people is a major act of obedience; ʿUmar reports the Prophet advised replacing a servant whose temperament does not suit the purchaser’s, since people have different temperaments, and forbade tormenting God’s servants.
rows.anchor: روى عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( من ابتاع شيئا من الخدم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet’s final words were to attend to prayer and those whom one’s right hand possesses.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان آخر كلامه : ( الصلاة وما ملكت أيمانكم )

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man stopped beating his servant when the servant invoked the Messenger; the Prophet said God had the greater right to protect a person seeking refuge, and warned the master of Hellfire before he freed the servant.
rows.anchor: وروي أنه كان رجل بالمدينة يضرب عبده ، فيقول العبد أعوذ بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kind treatment of enslaved people means not imposing what they cannot bear, avoiding harsh speech and dealing well with them, and providing the food and clothing they need.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الاحسان اليهم من وجوه : أحدها : أن لا يكلفهم ما لا طاقة لهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In pre-Islamic custom, enslaved women were mistreated by being forced into prostitution for earnings from their sexual services.
rows.anchor: وكانوا في الجاهلية يسيئون إلى المملوك فيكلفون الاماء البغاء

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say every living creature is owned, and kindness appropriate to each creature is a great act of obedience.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : كل حيوان فهو مملوك ، والاحسان إلى الكل بما يليق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the right hand is emphatic, as in saying that one’s foot walked or one’s hand took; he also cites the maxim that a hand is responsible for what it takes and God’s reference to what His hands made.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن ذكر اليمين تأكيد وهو كما يقال : مشت رجلك ، وأخذت يدك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the conceited person as one who is inflated in his own estimation and fails to fulfill anyone’s rights.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد بالمختال العظيم في نفسه الذي لا يقوم بحقوق أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fakhr is self-exaltation; the boastful person enumerates his merits out of arrogance and vaunting.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الفخر التطاول ، والفخور الذي يعدد مناقبه كبرا وتطاولا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the boastful person flaunts before God’s servants the kinds of favors God has bestowed on him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : هو الذي يفخر على عباد الله بما أعطاه الله من أنواع نعمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conceited person is unlikely to honor others’ rights; adding ‘boastful’ warns against honoring them merely for reputation, rather than solely in obedience to God.
rows.anchor: لأن المختال هو المتكبر ، وكل من كان متكبرا فانه قلما يقوم برعاية الحقوق

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj notes that the derivation of ikhtiyāl was discussed in the commentary on 3:14.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : وإنما ذكر الاختيال ههنا ، وذكرنا اشتقاق هذه اللفظة عند قوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ladun means ‘with’ or ‘in the presence of’ more specifically than ʿinda: one may have property ‘at’ another town, but ladā/ladunī implies it is present.
rows.anchor: لدن : بمعنى ( عند ) إلا أن ( لدن ) أكثر تمكينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He proposes that multiplying a good deed yields more of the same kind of bodily pleasures promised in Paradise, while the great reward from God’s presence is spiritual: the beatitude of vision and immersion in love and knowledge, granted through illumination of the purified soul.
rows.anchor: فذلك التضعيف إشارة إلى السعادة الجسمانية ، وهذا الأجر العظيم إشارة إلى السعادة الروحانية

words: فَكَيْفَ إِذَا جِئْنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةٍ بِشَهِيدٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing that God wrongs no one and rewards good beyond its due, the verse says messengers will testify, making the proof and reproach stronger, intensifying wrongdoers’ regret and increasing the obedient’s joy; it warns disbelievers and promises the obedient as in 4:40.
rows.anchor: وجه النظم هو أنه تعالى بين أن في الآخرة لا يجري على أحد ظلم ، وأنه تعالى يجازي المحسن على إحسانه

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the Prophet asked him to recite the Qur’an, explaining that he liked hearing it from someone else; when Ibn Masʿūd reached this verse, the Prophet wept and he stopped.
rows.anchor: روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لابن مسعود : ( إقرأ القرآن علي )

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says Muhammad’s community will testify that the messengers delivered their message, and the Messenger will testify concerning his community, as in the ‘middle community’ verse.
rows.anchor: وذكر السدي أن أمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم يشهدون للرسل بالبلاغ

rows.speaker: عيسى عليه السلام
rows.claim: Jesus’ statement that he witnessed his people only while among them illustrates testimony by those who observed each generation’s condition.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن عيسى عليه السلام أنه قال : { وكنت عليهم شهيدا ما دمت فيهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabs use ‘how will it be with you when…?’ for an anticipated event; here it asks how the people addressed by the Qur’an will fare when God calls each nation’s messenger and calls Muhammad to testify against them.
rows.anchor: من عادة العرب أنهم يقولون في الشيء الذي يتوقعونه : كيف بك إذا كان كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conjoining ‘disobeyed the Messenger’ to ‘disbelieved’ means the disobedience differs from disbelief, since a thing cannot be conjoined to itself.
rows.anchor: لأن عطف الشيء على نفسه غير جائز ، فوجب حمل عصيان الرسول على المعاصي المغايرة للكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse therefore indicates that unbelievers are addressed by Islam’s practical obligations and punished for those sins in addition to disbelief; otherwise mentioning their disobedience here would serve no purpose.
rows.anchor: إذا ثبت هذا فنقول : الآية دالة على أن الكفار مخاطبون بفروع الاسلام

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, and Abū ʿAmr read tusawwā with passive construction: tāʾ vowelled ḍamma and light sīn.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وأبو عمرو { تسوى } مضمومة التاء خفيفة السين

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read with fatḥa on tāʾ and doubled sīn, meaning ‘become level’; the tāʾ assimilates into the nearby sīn, a pattern also found at 27:47, 10:24, and 6:26.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر { تسوى } مفتوحة التاء مشددة السين بمعنى : تتسوى

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read with fatḥa on tāʾ and light sīn, dropping the tāʾ that Nāfiʿ assimilates.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي { لو تسوى } مفتوحة التاء والسين خفيفة

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: One interpretation is that they wish to be buried and covered by earth as the dead are.
rows.anchor: الأول : لو يدفنون فتسوى بهم الأرض كما تسوى بالموتى

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: A second interpretation is that they wish they had never been resurrected and had remained equal with the earth.
rows.anchor: والثاني : يودون أنهم لم يبعثوا وأنهم كانوا والأرض سواء

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: A third interpretation is that animals will be turned to dust, and the disbelievers will wish to share their state, as in 78:40.
rows.anchor: الثالث : تصير البهائم ترابا فيودون حالها كقوله : { الكافر ياليتنى كنت ترابا }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: If the clause continues the preceding wish, Ibn ʿAbbās says they wish earth would close over them and that they had not concealed Muhammad’s message, disbelieved in him, or acted hypocritically.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : ما قاله ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : يودون لو تنطبق عليهم الأرض ولم يكونوا كتموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another connected reading has polytheists first deny their shirk when they see Muslims forgiven; God then seals their mouths and their limbs testify to their deeds, so they wish they had been earth and had not denied the truth.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن المشركين لما رأوا يوم القيامة أن الله تعالى يغفر لأهل الاسلام ولا يغفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second exegetical approach treats this as a new sentence: their deeds are manifest to God, so they cannot possibly conceal them.
rows.anchor: الطريق الثاني في التأويل : أن هذا الكلام مستأنف ، فإن ما عملوه ظاهر عند الله ، فكيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statements that they will not conceal the truth and that they will deny being polytheists at 6:23 concern different stages of Judgment: some are silent, some speak and lie, some confess and ask to return, and finally their mouths are sealed while their limbs testify.
rows.anchor: أن مواطن القيامة كثيرة ، فموطن لا يتكلمون فيه وهو قوله : { فلا تسمع إلا همسا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reconciliation says the denial never actually occurs; it is only part of what they wish they had not done.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن هذا الكتمان غير واقع ، بل هو داخل في التمني على ما بينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third says they did not intend concealment: they spoke according to what they had thought, considering themselves right until the truth became clear.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أنهم لم يقصدوا الكتمان ، وإنما أخبروا على حسب ما توهموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One occasion report says ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf served food and drink to companions while wine was still permitted; after drinking, an imam garbled the recitation at Maghrib, prompting the verse. They then avoided wine at prayer times until sober, before its final prohibition in al-Māʾida.
rows.anchor: أكلوا وشربوا ، فلما ثلموا جاء وقت صلاة المغرب فقدموا أحدهم

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: When ʿUmar heard the ruling, he prayed that God issue a command about wine because it harms minds and property; the revelation of al-Māʾida came the next morning.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله عنه أنه لما بلغه ذلك قال : اللهم إن الخمر تضر بالعقول والأموال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives another occasion: before wine was forbidden, senior Companions drank and came to the mosque to pray with the Messenger, so God prohibited this.
rows.anchor: الثاني : قال ابن عباس : نزلت في جماعة من أكابر الصحابة قبل تحريم الخمر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود والحسن والشافعي
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, and al-Ḥasan take ‘prayer’ to mean the mosque, and al-Shāfiʿī adopts this view; it can mean ‘place of prayer’ by common ellipsis, as ṣalawāt means prayer sites at 22:40.
rows.anchor: المراد منه المسجد ، وهو قول ابن عباس وابن مسعود والحسن ، وإليه ذهب الشافعي

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: The majority take ṣalāt here to mean the prayer itself: do not perform it while intoxicated.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : وعليه الأكثرون : أن المراد بالصلاة في هذه الآية نفس الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ṣalāt means the mosque, the verse bars entering it drunk or while junub except to pass through, allowing a junub person to cross the mosque, as al-Shāfiʿī holds.
rows.anchor: يكون المعنى : لا تقربوا المسجد وأنتم سكارى ولا جنبا إلا عابري سبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ṣalāt means the prayer, the verse bars praying drunk or junub except for a traveling wayfarer, allowing a junub traveler unable to find water to pray by tayammum.
rows.anchor: والمراد بعابر السبيل المسافر ، فيكون هذا الاستثناء دليلا على أنه يجوز للجنب الاقدام على الصلاة

rows.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī’s adherents prefer the mosque reading because ‘approach’ naturally applies to a place, whereas it does not literally apply to the prayer itself.
rows.anchor: أنه قال : { لا تقربوا الصلواة } والقرب والبعد لا يصحان على نفس الصلاة على سبيل الحقيقة

rows.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
rows.claim: They argue the exception works under the mosque reading; under the prayer reading it fails because a sick nontraveler unable to use water may still pray by tayammum.
rows.anchor: أنا لو حملناه على ما قلنا لكان الاستثناء صحيحا ، أما لو حملناه على ما قلتم

rows.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
rows.claim: If the wayfarer means a junub traveler, the alternative reading requires unstated conditions about having water or needing tayammum; the mosque reading requires no such additions.
rows.anchor: فحينئذ يحتاج إلى إضمار هذا الاستثناء في الآية ، وإن لم يكن واجدا للماء لم يجز له الصلاة إلا مع التيمم

words: وَإِن كُنتُم مَّرْضَىٰٓ أَوْ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٍ
rows.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
rows.claim: They argue the travel and water ruling follows as a separate rule: readers prefer pausing at ‘until you wash,’ so the earlier exception should not depend on the later verse’s condition.
rows.anchor: والذي يؤكده أن القراء كلهم استحبوا الوقف عند قوله : { حتى تغتسلوا } ثم يستأنف قوله

rows.speaker: من نصر القول الثاني
rows.claim: Proponents of the prayer reading argue that ‘until you know what you say’ concerns prayer, which has prescribed speech, while no prescribed speech in the mosque is affected by drunkenness.
rows.anchor: ولمن نصر القول الثاني أن يقول : إن قوله تعالى : { حتى تعلموا ما تقولون } يدل على أن المراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mosque reading answers that people ordinarily go to the mosque for prayer, so whatever prevents prayer also counts as a reason not to go to the mosque.
rows.anchor: فما يخل بالصلاة كان كالمانع من الذهاب إلى المسجد

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says sukkārā is the plural of sakrān; adjectives on faʿlān take the plural patterns fuʿālā and fuʿālā, as in kasālā.
rows.anchor: الواحدي رحمه الله : السكارى جمع سكران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root sense of sakr is blocking a path: it describes stopping a water channel, a confused eye, or water diverted from its course; wine blocks reason from penetrating as it does in sobriety. At 15:15, vision is veiled from true perception.
rows.anchor: وأصل السكر في اللغة سد الطريق ، ومن ذلك سكر البثق وهو سده ، وسكرت عينه سكرا

rows.speaker: جمهور الصحابة والتابعين
rows.claim: The majority of Companions and Successors understand the word as intoxication from wine, the opposite of sobriety.
rows.anchor: المراد منه السكر من الخمر وهو نقيض الصحو ، وهو قول الجمهور من الصحابة والتابعين

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the word means sleep rather than wine intoxication: sleep blocks the channels of the spirit, preventing sight and hearing from reaching the body’s exterior.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الضحاك : وهو أنه ليس المراد منه سكر الخمر ، إنما المراد منه سكر النوم

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq’s line compares sleep to wine, supporting the use of sakr for sleep.
rows.anchor: من السير والادلاج يحسب انما سقاه الكرى في كل منزلة خمرا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk argues that the verse describes sleep because an unaware person cannot be charged with a duty; the Prophet’s report lifts the pen from children, the insane, and sleepers until they wake or recover.
rows.anchor: فهو قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( رفع القلم عن ثلاث عن الصبي حتى يبلغ وعن المجنون حتى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said that when someone grows drowsy during prayer, they should sleep until the drowsiness passes, lest they seek forgiveness while actually cursing themselves; al-Ḍaḥḥāk uses this to support the sleep interpretation.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( إذا نعس أحدكم وهو في الصلاة فليرقد حتى يذهب عنه النوم فإنه إذا صلى وهو ينعس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers wine intoxication: sakr literally means drunkenness from wine, while intoxication from passion, anger, fear, or sleep is figurative and normally qualified; he cites 50:19 and 22:2.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الصحيح هو القول الأول ، ويدل عليه وجهان : الأول : أن لفظ السكر حقيقة في السكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All exegetes agree the verse was revealed about wine, so that cause must be included; the command targets drinking that would impair understanding when prayer is due, not prayer by a person already unaware. The sleep hadith does not prove that sakr means sleep.
rows.anchor: أن جميع المفسرين اتفقوا على أن هذه الآية إنما نزلت في شرب الخمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some call the verse abrogated by al-Māʾida; al-Rāzī says the abrogated implication is that prayer becomes permitted once a drinker can understand, which the later total ban on wine removes.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : هذه الآية منسوخة بآية المائدة ، وأقول : الذي يمكن ادعاء النسخ فيه أنه يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A traveler who lacks water must use tayammum whether the journey is long or short.
rows.anchor: والآية تدل على أن المسافر إذا لم يجد الماء تيمم ، طال سفره أو قصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghāʾiṭ originally means a low, concealing place; people sought one to relieve themselves out of sight, and the bodily event later took the place’s name. Its plural is ghīṭān.
rows.anchor: والغائط المكان المطمئن من الأرض وجمعه الغيطان . وكان الرجل إذا أراد قضاء الحاجة طلب غائطا

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read lāmastum without alif, from lams; the other readers have the alif form, mulāmasa.
rows.anchor: المسألة الأولى : قرأ حمزة والكسائي : { لامستم } بغير ألف من اللمس ، والباقون { لامستم } بالألف من الملامسة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة وأبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Qatāda, and Abū Ḥanīfa take touching women to mean intercourse, since touching by hand does not invalidate ablution.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وقتادة ، وقول أبي حنيفة رضي الله عنه ، لأن اللمس باليد لا ينقض الطهارة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عمر والشعبي والنخعي والشافعي
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿUmar, al-Shaʿbī, al-Nakhaʿī, and al-Shāfiʿī understand the phrase as skin contact, with or without intercourse.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن مسعود وابن عمر والشعبي والنخعي وقول الشافعي رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers skin contact: lams literally means touching by hand, while restricting it to intercourse is figurative; mulāmasa also does not literally mean intercourse, so the two canonical readings should retain compatible literal senses.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذا القول أرجح من الأول ، وذلك لأن إحدى القراءتين هي قوله تعالى : { أو لامستم النساء } واللمس حقيقته المس باليد

rows.speaker: أنصار قول الجماع
rows.claim: Supporters of the intercourse interpretation cite Qur’anic euphemisms for intercourse at 2:37 and 58:3; Ibn ʿAbbās says God is modest and noble, veiling the meaning with ‘touching.’
rows.anchor: واحتج من قال : المراد باللمس الجماع ، بأن لفظ اللمس والمس وردا في القرآن بمعنى الجماع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that God is modest and noble and uses euphemism, calling sexual intimacy ‘touching.’
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنه قال : إن الله حيي كريم يعف ويكني ، فعبر عن المباشرة بالملامسة

rows.speaker: أنصار قول الجماع
rows.claim: They also argue that ‘coming from the place of need’ already covers minor impurity; if touching women also meant minor impurity, the verse would omit major impurity, so it must mean intercourse.
rows.anchor: وأيضا الحدث نوعان : الأصغر ، وهو المراد بقوله : { أو جاء أحد منكم من الغائط } فلو حملنا قوله
